trees.title: Compromise firmware/boot integrity or extract key material from an acquired unit
trees.description: Models the two realistic paths to defeating the RL-100's firmware/key-material protections once an attacker has physical possession of a unit (the selected SL-C 2 attacker profile), and the shared underlying gap (no hardware root of trust) that limits how far either path can be closed by software-only controls alone.

root.label: Compromise firmware/boot integrity or extract cryptographic key material

children.label: Defeat MCU readout protection (RDP) to gain low-level debug access
Acquire a physical unit (purchase, salvage, decommissioned device)
Bypass RDP via decapping, side-channel analysis, or voltage/clock fault injection
children.note: Directly targeted by CM-9 (JTAG/SWD production lockdown, REQC006). With RDP correctly enabled per AS-17, T-11's residual likelihood is rated 0; this step represents defeat of that control, not routine debug access.

children.label: Read out RAM/flash contents via the now-open debug interface
Bypass the firmware update-time signature/version check itself (T-13)
Obtain/forge a signature accepted by the verifier, or find an implementation bug in the check itself
children.note: CM-3 (update-time signature + anti-rollback check) is already implemented per AS-3; this step represents defeat of that control, not a routine firmware update.

children.label: Deliver the crafted image over IF-4 (Ethernet service) or IF-5 (USB-C), both already gated behind Service-level authentication
No hardware root of trust / secure boot below the update-time software checks (AS-9)
children.note: Without a hardware root of trust, an attacker who reaches low-level debug access (N-2) or defeats the software-only update check (N-8) is not blocked by any further layer. Accepted residual risk for T-11/T-13; no product control is currently planned to close this gap.

trees.title: Cause a crash, hang, or undefined behavior via a protocol parser
trees.description: Models the three alternative protocol entry points that can reach the same underlying parser-robustness gap, and the two controls (one already implemented, one still planned) that determine the actual consequence when a parser is hit.

root.label: Crash, hang, or otherwise disrupt the firmware/RTOS via malformed protocol input

children.label: Send a malformed Modbus RTU frame on the shared RS-485 segment (IF-3)
Send a malformed HART frame on the 4-20 mA loop (IF-2)
Send malformed/oversized data during an Ethernet service-interface session (IF-4)
Protocol parsers do not yet have demonstrated robustness against malformed/oversized/malicious input
children.note: All three entry points converge on this single underlying gap; closing it once (REQC005) addresses all of M-2/M-3/M-4 rather than needing a per-protocol fix.

children.label: Independent watchdog forces the defined fail-safe fault current during reset/restart
children.note: Already implemented (AS-18). Caps the safety-impact dimension at 1 regardless of which entry point triggers the crash/hang; does not reduce the availability impact of the outage itself, which remains dependent on CM-5 (still planned).
